identity.title: First Spectral Analysis of a Solar Plasma Eruption Using ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we use sub-band observations from the publicly available science verification (SV) data, whilst our methodology will also be applicable to regular ALMA data.

targets.name: Active region NOAA12470 region: XBP-coincident enhancement (box 1) and plasmoid ejection (box 2)

question.value: Can the logarithmic millimetre continuum gradient across ALMA Band 3 sub-bands be used to estimate optical thickness (and hence temperature/emission measure) of a solar plasmoid and an X-ray bright point enhancement?

evidence.quote: The aim of this study is to demonstrate how the logarithmic millimeter continuum gradient observed using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) may be used to estimate optical thickness in the solar atmosphere.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00020.SV.
The observation was conducted using ALMA Band 3 which has a central frequency of 100 GHz in the bandwidth of 84 – 116 GHz.
four constituent spectral windows of Band 3; 93, 95, 105 and 107 GHz
This observation was conducted with a reduced interferometer setup of 22x12 m and 9x7 m antennae
The observing beam for this observation was elliptical with a semi-major axis of 6.2$''$ and semi-minor axis of 2.3$''$
On the 17th of December 2015 ALMA observed a region near the large leading sunspot of active region NOAA12470
This dataset, along with other SV data sets, has been publicly released by the joint ALMA observatory
An SDO/AIA 304 Å image shows the context for the observation in Figure [2]
free-free Gaunt factor interpolated from the table of numerically calculated values given by (cite: 2014MNRAS.444..420V)

evidence.quote: we have adopted the quiet-Sun model C7 from (cite: 2008ApJS..175..229A) to give an example continuum spectrum for Band 3

method.value: Calibrate with SV reference scripts; synthesise images at 2 s cadence for full band and each of four spectral windows

evidence.quote: synthesise each image using the full bandwidth of Band 3 at a cadence of 2 s

validation.value: Replicated Shimojo et al. noise level of 11 K

evidence.quote: We replicate the 11 K noise level value presented by (cite: 2017ApJ...841L...5S)

method.value: Mean Tb in two boxes per time step; enhancement = enhanced minus background phase (N=29 steps each); noise from XX-YY, plus 5% flux-scale error

evidence.quote: As the number of timesteps in both the background and enhanced phases were kept equal at $N=29$
we have assumed a normally-distributed random uncertainty where the mean is zero and $3\sigma$ is equal to the 5% limit.

method.value: Bayesian linear regression of log E vs log nu with emcee

evidence.quote: we sampled it using a python implementation of the affine-invariant ensemble sampler for Markov-chain Monte-Carlo (MCMC) method (EMCEE)
We sampled using 100 chains, each with 1000 steps including tuning.

fitting.value: Normal likelihood in log space; uniform non-informative priors on gradient and intercept; 90% percentile intervals

evidence.quote: The prior distributions for the two desired fitting parameters, i.e spectral gradient and y-intercept, have been set as non-informative uniform distributions.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive optical thickness and plasma parameters

method.value: Intersect gradient confidence interval with diagnostic curve using alpha (1.04–1.09) and beta bounds; then derive T, EM, density

evidence.quote: Through plotting this curve and the confidence intervals of the fitted enhancement gradient it is possible to estimate the optical thickness/optical thickness regime

assumptions.value: Isothermal plasma; C7 model background; purely hydrogen plasma; background Tb 7300±100 K

evidence.quote: We assume a purely hydrogen plasma and a solely thermal bremsstrahlung emission mechanism.

validation.value: Single-dish images checked to support the assumed background value

evidence.quote: This assumption was checked by viewing the ALMA single-dish images during the observation

findings_qualitative.value: Both enhancements lie in the transition between optically thin and thick plasma; plasmoid results favour cool optically thick core model of Shimojo et al.

evidence.quote: where both lie entirely in the transition region between optically thin and optically thick plasma.

evidence.quote: Sub-band analysis of the logarithmic mm continuum brightness temperature spectrum proves to be a potentially powerful technique for diagnosing plasma optical thickness

limitations_admitted.value: Flux scale accuracy is the largest uncertainty; background gradient uncertainty not included; isothermal assumption
